verses.1:1: In the eighth month, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo the prophet, saying,
verses.1:2: "The LORD was fiercely angry with your fathers.
verses.1:3: Therefore say to them, 'Thus says the LORD of hosts: Return to Me, declares the LORD of hosts, and I will return to you, says the LORD of hosts.
verses.1:4: Do not be like your fathers, to whom the former prophets cried out, saying, "Thus says the LORD of hosts: Turn now from your evil ways and your evil deeds." Yet they did not listen nor give heed to Me, declares the LORD.
verses.1:5: Your fathers, where are they? And the prophets, do they live forever?
verses.1:6: Yet My words and My statutes, which I commanded My servants the prophets, did they not overtake your fathers? So they repented and said, "Just as the LORD of hosts purposed to do to us, according to our ways and according to our deeds, so He has dealt with us."'"
verses.1:7: On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, which is the month of Shebat, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo the prophet, saying:
verses.1:8: I saw by night, and behold, a man was riding upon a red horse, standing among the myrtle trees in the deep hollow; and behind him were horses: red, sorrel, and white.
verses.1:9: Then I said, "My lord, what are these?" And the angel who spoke with me said to me, "I will show you what these are."
verses.1:10: And the man who stood among the myrtle trees answered and said, "These are the ones whom the LORD has sent to walk to and fro through the earth."
verses.1:11: Then they answered the Angel of the LORD, who stood among the myrtle trees, and said, "We have walked to and fro through the earth, and behold, all the earth is sitting still and at rest."
verses.1:12: Then the Angel of the LORD answered and said, "O LORD of hosts, how long will You not have mercy on Jerusalem and on the cities of Judah, against which You have had indignation these seventy years?"
verses.1:13: And the LORD answered the angel who spoke with me with good words, words of comfort.
verses.1:14: So the angel who spoke with me said to me, "Proclaim, saying, 'Thus says the LORD of hosts: I am zealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with great zeal.
verses.1:15: And I am exceedingly angry with the nations that are at ease; for I was only a little angry, yet they furthered the calamity.
verses.1:16: Therefore thus says the LORD: I have returned to Jerusalem with mercy; My house shall be built in it, declares the LORD of hosts, and a measuring line shall be stretched out over Jerusalem.'
verses.1:17: Proclaim yet again, saying, 'Thus says the LORD of hosts: My cities shall again overflow with prosperity; and the LORD will again comfort Zion, and will again choose Jerusalem.'"
verses.2:1: Then I lifted up my eyes and looked, and behold, there were four horns.
verses.2:2: And I said to the angel who spoke with me, "What are these?" And he said to me, "These are the horns that have scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem."
verses.2:3: Then the LORD showed me four craftsmen.
verses.2:4: And I said, "What are these coming to do?" So he spoke, saying, "These are the horns that scattered Judah, so that no man lifted up his head; yet these have come to terrify them, to cast down the horns of the nations that lifted up their horn against the land of Judah to scatter it."
verses.2:5: Then I lifted up my eyes and looked, and behold, a man with a measuring line in his hand.
verses.2:6: So I said, "Where are you going?" And he said to me, "To measure Jerusalem, to see what is its breadth and what is its length."
verses.2:7: And behold, the angel who spoke with me went out, and another angel came out to meet him,
verses.2:8: and said to him, "Run, speak to that young man, saying, 'Jerusalem shall be inhabited as unwalled villages, because of the multitude of men and livestock in its midst.
verses.2:9: For I, declares the LORD, will be to it a wall of fire all around, and I will be the glory in its midst.'"
verses.2:10: "Up! Up! Flee from the land of the north," declares the LORD, "for I have spread you abroad like the four winds of the heavens," declares the LORD.
verses.2:11: "Up, Zion! Escape, you who dwell with the daughter of Babylon."
verses.2:12: For thus says the LORD of hosts: "After glory He has sent Me to the nations that plunder you; for whoever touches you touches the apple of His eye.
verses.2:13: For behold, I will shake My hand over them, and they shall become plunder for their servants. Then you shall know that the LORD of hosts has sent Me."
verses.2:14: "Sing and rejoice, O daughter of Zion! For behold, I am coming, and I will dwell in your midst," declares the LORD.
verses.2:15: "And many nations shall be joined to the LORD in that day, and they shall become My people. And I will dwell in your midst, and you shall know that the LORD of hosts has sent Me to you."
verses.2:16: And the LORD shall inherit Judah as His portion in the holy land, and shall again choose Jerusalem.
verses.2:17: Be silent, all flesh, before the LORD, for He has roused Himself from His holy habitation.
verses.3:1: Then he showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the Angel of the LORD, and Satan standing at his right hand to accuse him.
verses.3:2: And the LORD said to Satan, "The LORD rebuke you, Satan! Even the LORD who has chosen Jerusalem rebuke you! Is this not a firebrand snatched from the fire?"
verses.3:3: Now Joshua was clothed with filthy garments, and was standing before the Angel.
verses.3:4: Then He answered and spoke to those who stood before Him, saying, "Take off the filthy garments from him." And to him He said, "See, I have removed your iniquity from you, and I will clothe you with stately robes."
verses.3:5: And I said, "Let them set a clean turban upon his head." So they set the clean turban upon his head and clothed him with garments, while the Angel of the LORD stood by.
verses.3:6: Then the Angel of the LORD solemnly charged Joshua, saying,
verses.3:7: "Thus says the LORD of hosts: If you will walk in My ways, and if you will keep My charge, then you shall also govern My house and also guard My courts, and I will grant you places to walk among these who stand here.
verses.3:8: Hear now, O Joshua the high priest, you and your companions who sit before you, for they are men of a sign; for behold, I am bringing forth My Servant the Branch.
verses.3:9: For behold, the stone that I have set before Joshua: upon one stone are seven eyes. Behold, I will engrave its inscription, declares the LORD of hosts, and I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day.
verses.3:10: In that day, declares the LORD of hosts, every one of you shall invite his neighbor under the vine and under the fig tree."
verses.4:1: Then the angel who spoke with me returned and awakened me, like a man who is roused from his sleep.
verses.4:2: And he said to me, "What do you see?" And I said, "I have looked, and behold, a lampstand entirely of gold with its bowl upon its top, and its seven lamps upon it, with seven and seven pipes for the lamps that are upon its top,
verses.4:3: and two olive trees beside it, one at the right of the bowl and one at its left."
verses.4:4: Then I answered and spoke to the angel who spoke with me, saying, "What are these, my lord?"
verses.4:5: And the angel who spoke with me answered and said to me, "Do you not know what these are?" And I said, "No, my lord."
verses.4:6: Then he answered and said to me, "This is the word of the LORD to Zerubbabel: 'Not by might, nor by strength, but by My Spirit,' says the LORD of hosts.
verses.4:7: Who are you, O great mountain? Before Zerubbabel you shall become a plain! And he shall bring forth the chief stone amid shouts of 'Grace, grace to it!'"
verses.4:8: Moreover, the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
verses.4:9: "The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house, and his hands shall also complete it. Then you shall know that the LORD of hosts has sent me to you.
verses.4:10: For who has despised the day of small things? Yet these seven shall rejoice when they behold the plummet in the hand of Zerubbabel—they are the eyes of the LORD, which range to and fro throughout all the earth."
verses.4:11: Then I answered and said to him, "What are these two olive trees, on the right of the lampstand and on its left?"
verses.4:12: And I answered a second time and said to him, "What are these two olive branches beside the two golden pipes that pour out the golden oil from themselves?"
verses.4:13: Then he spoke to me, saying, "Do you not know what these are?" And I said, "No, my lord."
verses.4:14: So he said, "These are the two anointed ones, who stand beside the Lord of all the earth."
verses.5:1: Then I turned and lifted up my eyes, and looked, and behold, a flying scroll.
verses.5:2: And he said to me, "What do you see?" So I answered, "I see a flying scroll; its length is twenty cubits and its breadth is ten cubits."
verses.5:3: Then he said to me, "This is the curse that goes forth over the face of the whole earth: for every thief shall be purged away according to this side of it, and every swearer shall be purged away according to that side of it.
verses.5:4: 'I have sent it forth,' says the LORD of hosts, 'and it shall enter the house of the thief and the house of the one who swears falsely by My name. It shall abide in the midst of his house and consume it, both its timber and its stones.'"
verses.5:5: Then the angel who spoke with me came forward and said to me, "Lift up your eyes now, and see what this is that goes forth."
verses.5:6: And I said, "What is it?" And he said, "This is the ephah that goes forth." He also said, "This is their appearance throughout all the earth."
verses.5:7: And behold, a round disk of lead was lifted up, and there was a woman sitting in the midst of the ephah.
verses.5:8: Then he said, "This is Wickedness!" And he thrust her down into the midst of the ephah, and cast the leaden weight upon its mouth.
verses.5:9: Then I lifted up my eyes and looked, and behold, two women came forth with the wind in their wings, for they had wings like the wings of a stork; and they lifted up the ephah between the earth and the heavens.
verses.5:10: So I said to the angel who spoke with me, "Where are they carrying the ephah?"
verses.5:11: And he said to me, "To build a house for it in the land of Shinar; and when it is prepared, it shall be set down there upon its own base."
verses.6:1: Then I turned and lifted up my eyes, and looked, and behold, four chariots were coming forth from between two mountains, and the mountains were mountains of bronze.
verses.6:2: With the first chariot were red horses, and with the second chariot black horses,
verses.6:3: with the third chariot white horses, and with the fourth chariot dappled horses, strong steeds.
verses.6:4: Then I answered and said to the angel who spoke with me, "What are these, my lord?"
verses.6:5: And the angel answered and said to me, "These are the four spirits of heaven, going forth after presenting themselves before the Lord of all the earth.
verses.6:6: The one with the black horses is going forth to the north country, and the white ones have gone forth after them, while the dappled ones have gone forth to the south country."
verses.6:7: Then the strong steeds went forth and sought to go, to walk to and fro through the earth. And He said, "Go, walk to and fro through the earth." So they walked to and fro through the earth.
verses.6:8: Then He called out to me and spoke to me, saying, "See, those who go forth to the north country have given rest to My Spirit in the north country."
verses.6:9: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
verses.6:10: "Take from the exiles—from Heldai, from Tobijah, and from Jedaiah—and come on that same day, and enter the house of Josiah the son of Zephaniah, who have come from Babylon.
verses.6:11: Take silver and gold, make crowns, and set them upon the head of Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest.
verses.6:12: And speak to him, saying, 'Thus says the LORD of hosts: Behold, a man whose name is Branch! From his own place he shall branch out, and he shall build the temple of the LORD.
verses.6:13: Indeed, he shall build the temple of the LORD, and he shall bear majesty, and shall sit and rule upon his throne. And he shall be a priest upon his throne, and the counsel of peace shall be between the two of them.'
verses.6:14: Now the crowns shall be for Helem, for Tobijah, for Jedaiah, and for Hen the son of Zephaniah, as a memorial in the temple of the LORD.
verses.6:15: And those who are far off shall come and build in the temple of the LORD. Then you shall know that the LORD of hosts has sent me to you. And this shall come to pass if you diligently obey the voice of the LORD your God."
verses.7:1: Now it came to pass in the fourth year of King Darius that the word of the LORD came to Zechariah on the fourth day of the ninth month, in Chislev.
verses.7:2: Then Bethel sent Sharezer and Regem-Melech and his men to seek the favor of the LORD,
verses.7:3: to speak to the priests who belong to the house of the LORD of hosts, and to the prophets, saying, "Should I weep in the fifth month and abstain, as I have done these many years?"
verses.7:4: Then the word of the LORD of hosts came to me, saying,
verses.7:5: "Speak to all the people of the land and to the priests, saying, 'When you fasted and lamented in the fifth and in the seventh months during these seventy years, did you indeed fast for Me—for Me?
verses.7:6: And when you ate and when you drank, were you not the ones who ate, and you the ones who drank?
verses.7:7: Should you not have heard the words which the LORD proclaimed through the former prophets, when Jerusalem was inhabited and at ease, with her cities around her, and the South and the Lowland were inhabited?'"
verses.7:8: Then the word of the LORD came to Zechariah, saying,
verses.7:9: "Thus says the LORD of hosts, saying, 'Administer true justice, and show lovingkindness and compassion, each man to his brother.
verses.7:10: Do not oppress the widow or the fatherless, the sojourner or the poor, and let none of you devise evil in your hearts against his brother.'
verses.7:11: But they refused to pay heed; they turned a stubborn shoulder and made their ears dull so that they would not hear.
verses.7:12: Indeed, they made their hearts as hard as flint, refusing to hear the law and the words which the LORD of hosts had sent by His Spirit through the former prophets. Therefore great wrath came from the LORD of hosts.
verses.7:13: Therefore it came to pass that just as He called and they did not hear, 'so they shall call and I will not hear,' says the LORD of hosts.
verses.7:14: 'And I scattered them with a whirlwind among all the nations which they did not know. Thus the land became desolate behind them, with no one passing through or returning; for they turned the pleasant land into a desolation.'"
verses.8:1: Then the word of the LORD of hosts came, saying:
verses.8:2: Thus says the LORD of hosts: "I am jealous for Zion with great jealousy, and with great wrath I am jealous for her."
verses.8:3: Thus says the LORD: "I have returned to Zion and will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem. Jerusalem shall be called the City of Truth, and the mountain of the LORD of hosts, the Holy Mountain."
verses.8:4: Thus says the LORD of hosts: "Old men and old women shall again sit in the squares of Jerusalem, each one with his staff in his hand because of great age.
verses.8:5: And the squares of the city shall be filled with boys and girls playing in its squares."
verses.8:6: Thus says the LORD of hosts: "If it is marvelous in the eyes of the remnant of this people in those days, will it also be marvelous in My eyes?" declares the LORD of hosts.
verses.8:7: Thus says the LORD of hosts: "Behold, I will save My people from the land of the east and from the land of the setting sun;
verses.8:8: and I will bring them back, and they shall dwell in the midst of Jerusalem. They shall be My people, and I will be their God, in truth and in righteousness."
verses.8:9: Thus says the LORD of hosts: "Let your hands be strong, you who in these days hear these words from the mouth of the prophets who were present on the day the foundation of the house of the LORD of hosts was laid, that the temple might be built.
verses.8:10: For before those days there were no wages for man, nor any hire for beast; there was no peace from the adversary for him who went out or came in, for I set all mankind, every man against his neighbor.
verses.8:11: But now I will not be to the remnant of this people as in the former days," declares the LORD of hosts.
verses.8:12: "For there shall be a sowing of peace: the vine shall yield its fruit, the land shall yield its produce, and the heavens shall give their dew; and I will cause the remnant of this people to inherit all these things.
verses.8:13: And it shall come to pass that just as you were a curse among the nations, O house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will save you, and you shall be a blessing. Do not fear; let your hands be strong."
verses.8:14: For thus says the LORD of hosts: "Just as I purposed to bring calamity upon you when your fathers provoked Me to wrath," says the LORD of hosts, "and I did not relent,
verses.8:15: so again in these days I have purposed to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. Do not fear.
verses.8:16: These are the things which you shall do: Speak the truth, each man to his neighbor; administer judgments of truth and peace in your gates.
verses.8:17: Let none of you devise evil in your hearts against his neighbor, and do not love a false oath; for all these are things that I hate," declares the LORD.
verses.8:18: Then the word of the LORD of hosts came to me, saying:
verses.8:19: Thus says the LORD of hosts: "The fast of the fourth month, the fast of the fifth, the fast of the seventh, and the fast of the tenth shall become joy and gladness and cheerful feasts for the house of Judah. Therefore love truth and peace."
verses.8:20: Thus says the LORD of hosts: "Peoples shall yet come, even the inhabitants of many cities;
verses.8:21: and the inhabitants of one city shall go to another, saying, 'Let us go at once to implore the favor of the LORD and to seek the LORD of hosts. I myself will go also.'
verses.8:22: Indeed, many peoples and mighty nations shall come to seek the LORD of hosts in Jerusalem, and to implore the favor of the LORD."
verses.8:23: Thus says the LORD of hosts: "In those days ten men from every tongue of the nations shall take hold—yes, they shall take hold of the robe of a Jewish man, saying, 'Let us go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.'"
verses.9:1: The burden of the word of the LORD is against the land of Hadrach, and Damascus is its resting place—for the eye of mankind and of all the tribes of Israel is toward the LORD—
verses.9:2: and against Hamath also, which borders upon it, and against Tyre and Sidon, though they are exceedingly wise.
verses.9:3: Tyre has built herself a stronghold, and heaped up silver like the dust, and fine gold like the mire of the streets.
verses.9:4: Behold, the Lord will dispossess her and strike down her power in the sea, and she herself shall be consumed by fire.
verses.9:5: Ashkelon shall see it and fear; Gaza also shall writhe in great anguish, and Ekron, for her hope has been put to shame. The king shall perish from Gaza, and Ashkelon shall not be inhabited.
verses.9:6: A mixed people shall dwell in Ashdod, and I will cut off the pride of the Philistines.
verses.9:7: I will remove his blood from his mouth and his abominations from between his teeth. Then he also shall remain as a remnant for our God; he shall be like a clan in Judah, and Ekron like a Jebusite.
verses.9:8: Then I will encamp at My house as a guard against any who pass by and return, and no oppressor shall overrun them anymore; for now I have seen with My own eyes.
verses.9:9: Rejoice exceedingly, O daughter of Zion! Shout aloud, O daughter of Jerusalem! Behold, your King comes to you; righteous and victorious is He, humble and mounted upon a donkey, even upon a colt, the foal of a she-donkey.
verses.9:10: I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim and the horse from Jerusalem, and the bow of war shall be cut off. He shall speak peace to the nations, and His dominion shall extend from sea to sea, and from the River to the ends of the earth.
verses.9:11: As for you also, because of the blood of your covenant, I have set your captives free from the pit in which there is no water.
verses.9:12: Return to the stronghold, O prisoners of hope! Even this very day I declare that I will restore double to you.
verses.9:13: For I have bent Judah for Myself as a bow and fitted Ephraim to it; I will rouse your sons, O Zion, against your sons, O Greece, and I will make you like the sword of a mighty warrior.
verses.9:14: Then the LORD will appear over them, and His arrow will flash forth like lightning; the Lord GOD will sound the trumpet and march in the whirlwinds of the south.
verses.9:15: The LORD of hosts will shield them; they shall devour and subdue the slingstones. They shall drink and roar as with wine, and they shall be filled like the sacrificial bowls, like the corners of the altar.
verses.9:16: On that day the LORD their God will save them as the flock of His people; for like the jewels of a crown, they shall gleam over His land.
verses.9:17: For how great is His goodness, and how great is His beauty! Grain shall make the young men flourish, and new wine the maidens.
verses.10:1: Ask rain from the LORD in the time of the latter rain; the LORD makes the storm clouds, and He will give them showers of rain, to every man grass in the field.
verses.10:2: For the household idols speak deceit, and the diviners envision falsehood; they tell empty dreams, and they offer comfort in vain. Therefore they wander like sheep; they are afflicted, because there is no shepherd.
verses.10:3: "My anger is kindled against the shepherds, and I will punish the male goats; for the LORD of hosts has visited His flock, the house of Judah, and He will make them like His majestic warhorse in battle.
verses.10:4: From him shall come the cornerstone, from him the tent peg, from him the battle bow, from him every ruler together.
verses.10:5: They shall be like mighty warriors, trampling in the mire of the streets in the battle; they shall fight, because the LORD is with them, and the riders on horses shall be put to shame.
verses.10:6: I will strengthen the house of Judah, and I will save the house of Joseph; I will bring them back, because I have compassion on them, and they shall be as though I had not cast them off; for I am the LORD their God, and I will answer them.
verses.10:7: Ephraim shall be like a mighty warrior, and their heart shall rejoice as with wine; their children also shall see it and be glad, and their heart shall exult in the LORD.
verses.10:8: I will whistle for them and gather them in, for I have redeemed them; and they shall multiply as they have multiplied before.
verses.10:9: Though I sow them among the peoples, in distant lands they shall remember Me; they shall live with their children and return.
verses.10:10: I will bring them back from the land of Egypt and gather them from Assyria; I will bring them to the land of Gilead and Lebanon, until no more room is found for them.
verses.10:11: He shall pass through the sea of distress and strike the waves in the sea, and all the depths of the Nile shall dry up; the pride of Assyria shall be brought down, and the scepter of Egypt shall depart.
verses.10:12: I will strengthen them in the LORD, and in His name they shall walk," declares the LORD.
verses.11:1: Open your doors, O Lebanon, that fire may devour your cedars.
verses.11:2: Wail, O cypress, for the cedar has fallen, because the mighty ones are laid waste! Wail, O oaks of Bashan, for the impenetrable forest has come down!
verses.11:3: The sound of the wailing of the shepherds, for their glory is laid waste! The sound of the roaring of young lions, for the pride of the Jordan is laid waste!
verses.11:4: Thus says the LORD my God: "Shepherd the flock for slaughter,
verses.11:5: whose buyers slay them and are not held guilty, and those who sell them say, 'Blessed be the LORD, for I have become rich!' and their own shepherds have no pity on them.
verses.11:6: For I will no longer have pity on the inhabitants of the land," declares the LORD. "Behold, I am delivering mankind, every man into the hand of his neighbor and into the hand of his king; they shall crush the land, and I will not rescue them from their hand."
verses.11:7: So I shepherded the flock for slaughter, indeed the afflicted of the flock. And I took for myself two staffs: the one I called Favor, and the other I called Union; and I shepherded the flock.
verses.11:8: I cut off the three shepherds in one month; my soul grew impatient with them, and their soul also detested me.
verses.11:9: Then I said, "I will not shepherd you. Let what is dying die, and let what is to be cut off be cut off; and let those that remain each devour the flesh of her neighbor."
verses.11:10: And I took my staff Favor and broke it in two, to annul my covenant which I had made with all the peoples.
verses.11:11: So it was annulled on that day, and thus the afflicted of the flock who were watching me knew that it was the word of the LORD.
verses.11:12: Then I said to them, "If it is good in your eyes, give me my wages; and if not, refrain." So they weighed out as my wages thirty pieces of silver.
verses.11:13: And the LORD said to me, "Cast it to the potter—that magnificent price at which I was valued by them!" So I took the thirty pieces of silver and cast them into the house of the LORD, to the potter.
verses.11:14: Then I broke my second staff, Union, in two, to annul the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.
verses.11:15: And the LORD said to me, "Take for yourself once more the equipment of a foolish shepherd.
verses.11:16: For behold, I am raising up a shepherd in the land who will not attend to the perishing, nor seek the young, nor heal the injured, nor nourish the sound; instead, he will devour the flesh of the fat ones and tear off their hooves."
verses.11:17: Woe to the worthless shepherd who forsakes the flock! A sword be upon his arm and upon his right eye! His arm shall completely wither, and his right eye shall be utterly darkened!
verses.12:1: The burden of the word of the LORD concerning Israel. Thus declares the LORD, who stretches out the heavens, lays the foundation of the earth, and forms the spirit of man within him:
verses.12:2: "Behold, I am making Jerusalem a cup of staggering to all the surrounding peoples, and Judah also shall be in the siege against Jerusalem.
verses.12:3: And it shall come to pass in that day that I will make Jerusalem a burdensome stone for all the peoples; all who lift it shall grievously lacerate themselves, and all the nations of the earth shall gather against her.
verses.12:4: In that day," declares the LORD, "I will strike every horse with panic and its rider with madness; I will open My eyes upon the house of Judah, and every horse of the peoples I will strike with blindness.
verses.12:5: Then the chiefs of Judah shall say in their heart, 'The inhabitants of Jerusalem are a strength to me through the LORD of hosts, their God.'
verses.12:6: In that day I will make the chiefs of Judah like a firepot among wood and like a flaming torch among sheaves; they shall devour all the surrounding peoples on the right hand and on the left, while Jerusalem shall again dwell in her own place, in Jerusalem.
verses.12:7: The LORD will save the tents of Judah first, so that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem may not be exalted above Judah.
verses.12:8: In that day the LORD will shield the inhabitants of Jerusalem; the feeble one among them in that day shall be like David, and the house of David shall be like God, like the Angel of the LORD before them.
verses.12:9: And it shall come to pass in that day that I will seek to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem.
verses.12:10: And I will pour out upon the house of David and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem a spirit of grace and supplications; and they shall look upon Me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for Him as one mourns for an only child, and grieve bitterly for Him as one grieves bitterly for a firstborn.
verses.12:11: In that day the mourning in Jerusalem shall be great, like the mourning of Hadad-Rimmon in the plain of Megiddo.
verses.12:12: And the land shall mourn, each family by itself: the family of the house of David by itself, and their wives by themselves; the family of the house of Nathan by itself, and their wives by themselves;
verses.12:13: the family of the house of Levi by itself, and their wives by themselves; the family of the Shimeites by itself, and their wives by themselves;
verses.12:14: all the remaining families, each family by itself, and their wives by themselves."
verses.13:1: In that day there shall be a fountain opened for the house of David and for the inhabitants of Jerusalem, for sin and for impurity.
verses.13:2: "And it shall come to pass in that day," declares the LORD of hosts, "that I will cut off the names of the idols from the land, and they shall be remembered no more; and I will also cause the prophets and the spirit of uncleanness to depart from the land."
verses.13:3: And it shall come to pass, if any man still prophesies, then his father and his mother who brought him forth shall say to him, "You shall not live, for you have spoken falsehood in the name of the LORD." And his father and his mother who brought him forth shall pierce him through when he prophesies.
verses.13:4: And it shall come to pass in that day that the prophets shall be ashamed, each man of his vision when he prophesies; neither shall they wear a mantle of hair in order to deceive.
verses.13:5: But he shall say, "I am no prophet; I am a man who tills the ground, for a man acquired me from my youth."
verses.13:6: And one shall say to him, "What are these wounds between your hands?" And he shall say, "Those with which I was struck in the house of those who love me."
verses.13:7: "Awake, O sword, against My shepherd, and against the man who is My associate," declares the LORD of hosts. "Strike the shepherd, and the flock shall be scattered; and I will turn My hand against the little ones."
verses.13:8: "And it shall come to pass in all the land," declares the LORD, "that two parts in it shall be cut off and perish, but the third shall remain in it.
verses.13:9: And I will bring the third part into the fire, and refine them as silver is refined, and test them as gold is tested. They shall call upon My name, and I will answer them. I will say, 'They are My people,' and they shall say, 'The LORD is my God.'"
verses.14:1: Behold, a day is coming for the LORD, and your spoil shall be divided in your midst.
verses.14:2: For I will gather all the nations against Jerusalem to battle; and the city shall be captured, the houses plundered, and the women violated. Half of the city shall go forth into exile, but the remnant of the people shall not be cut off from the city.
verses.14:3: Then the LORD shall go forth and fight against those nations, as on the day He fights in the day of battle.
verses.14:4: And in that day His feet shall stand upon the Mount of Olives, which lies before Jerusalem on the east. And the Mount of Olives shall be split in half from east to west into an exceedingly great valley; and half of the mountain shall move toward the north, and half of it toward the south.
verses.14:5: And you shall flee through the valley of My mountains, for the valley of the mountains shall reach to Azal; yes, you shall flee just as you fled from before the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah. Then the LORD my God shall come, and all the holy ones with You.
verses.14:6: And it shall come to pass in that day that there shall be no light, neither brightness nor frost.
verses.14:7: And it shall be one day, known to the LORD—neither day nor night—and it shall come to pass that at evening time there shall be light.
verses.14:8: And it shall come to pass in that day that living waters shall flow forth from Jerusalem, half of them toward the eastern sea and half of them toward the western sea; in summer and in winter it shall be so.
verses.14:9: And the LORD shall become King over all the earth; in that day the LORD shall be one, and His name one.
verses.14:10: All the land shall be turned into a plain from Geba to Rimmon south of Jerusalem; and Jerusalem shall be lifted up and abide in her place, from the Gate of Benjamin to the place of the First Gate, to the Corner Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel to the king's winepresses.
verses.14:11: And people shall dwell in her, and there shall no longer be utter destruction; and Jerusalem shall dwell in security.
verses.14:12: And this shall be the plague with which the LORD shall strike all the peoples who have waged war against Jerusalem: their flesh shall rot away while they still stand upon their feet, their eyes shall rot in their sockets, and their tongues shall rot in their mouths.
verses.14:13: And it shall come to pass in that day that a great tumult from the LORD shall be among them; and each man shall seize the hand of his neighbor, and his hand shall rise up against the hand of his neighbor.
verses.14:14: And Judah also shall fight at Jerusalem; and the wealth of all the surrounding nations shall be gathered together—gold and silver and garments in exceedingly great abundance.
verses.14:15: And thus shall be the plague upon the horse, the mule, the camel, and the donkey, and upon all the beasts that shall be in those camps, even as this plague.
verses.14:16: And it shall come to pass that all who remain of all the nations that came against Jerusalem shall go up year by year to worship the King, the LORD of hosts, and to observe the Feast of Tabernacles.
verses.14:17: And it shall come to pass that whoever among the families of the earth does not go up to Jerusalem to worship the King, the LORD of hosts, upon them there shall be no rain.
verses.14:18: And if the family of Egypt does not go up and does not enter, then upon them there shall be no rain; there shall be the plague with which the LORD shall strike the nations that do not go up to observe the Feast of Tabernacles.
verses.14:19: This shall be the punishment of Egypt and the punishment of all the nations that do not go up to observe the Feast of Tabernacles.
verses.14:20: In that day there shall be upon the bells of the horses, "HOLINESS TO THE LORD." And the pots in the house of the LORD shall be like the basins before the altar.
verses.14:21: And every pot in Jerusalem and in Judah shall be holy to the LORD of hosts; and all those who sacrifice shall come and take of them and boil in them. And there shall no longer be a Canaanite in the house of the LORD of hosts in that day.

notes.1:4: The Qere reads 'uma'alelekem' ("and your deeds"), whereas the Ketiv has the longer orthographic form 'uma'alilekem' with the same meaning.
notes.1:8: The Hebrew 'metsulah' denotes a low-lying hollow, glen, or ravine, and 'seruqqim' refers to sorrel or reddish-brown horses.
notes.1:16: The Qere reads 'weqaw' ("and a measuring line"), while the Ketiv has the alternate spelling 'weqaweh' with the same sense.
notes.2:1: Following the Masoretic Hebrew versification, chapter 2 begins with the vision of the four horns and four craftsmen; verses 2:1-4 correspond to 1:18-21 and verses 2:5-17 correspond to 2:1-13 in many English Bibles.
notes.2:12: The terse Hebrew phrase 'achar kavod' ("After glory") is variously understood as "following His manifestation of glory" or "for the sake of His honor."
notes.2:17: The interjection 'has' ("Be silent") is a solemn liturgical summons to reverent stillness before the LORD's decisive action.
notes.3:1: The Hebrew pairs the noun 'hassatan' ("Satan" or "the Adversary") with the cognate verb 'lesitno' ("to accuse him" or "to act as adversary against him").
notes.3:5: The Masoretic Hebrew reads first-person 'wa'omar' ("And I said"), portraying Zechariah himself speaking aloud in the heavenly council.
notes.3:7: The rare Hebrew form 'mahlekim' ("places to walk") denotes free right of access among the angelic attendants standing in the divine court.
notes.3:8: The Hebrew 'Tsemach' ("Branch" or "Shoot") is a royal messianic title echoing Jeremiah 23:5 and 33:15.
notes.4:2: The Hebrew ketiv reads "he said," while the qere (followed here) reads "I said." The Hebrew idiom "seven and seven" likely indicates seven pipes supplying each of the seven lamps.
notes.4:10: "Plummet" translates the Hebrew phrase literally meaning "the stone of tin," referring to a builder's plumb weight.
notes.4:12: "Golden oil" literally reads "the gold" in Hebrew, referring to fresh golden olive oil.
notes.4:14: "Anointed ones" renders the Hebrew idiom literally meaning "sons of fresh oil."
notes.5:3: "Purged away" translates a Hebrew verb meaning to be cleaned out or swept away in judgment according to the curse inscribed on both sides of the scroll.
notes.5:6: An ephah was a dry-measure basket holding roughly half a bushel. "Their appearance" literally reads "their eye" in the Masoretic Text, denoting likeness or aspect, whereas some ancient versions read "their iniquity."
notes.5:11: Shinar is the ancient biblical name for the plain of Babylonia.
notes.6:3: The Hebrew adjective rendered "strong steeds" here and in verse 7 denotes strength, though some interpreters take it as a horse color such as bay or reddish.
notes.6:5: The Hebrew noun rendered "spirits" can also mean "winds."
notes.6:13: The Hebrew clause may also be translated "there shall be a priest beside his throne," so that "the two of them" refers either to the royal and priestly offices united in one figure or to the Branch and the priest together.
notes.6:14: The plural noun "crowns" is paired with a singular verb in Hebrew, suggesting an elaborate composite crown. The Masoretic Text preserves the forms Helem and Hen here where verse 10 reads Heldai and Josiah.
notes.7:2: The Hebrew syntax allows reading Bethel either as the subject sending the delegation or as part of a compound personal name, Bethel-Sharezer; the Masoretic accentuation favors taking Bethel as the sender.
notes.7:7: "The South" translates the Hebrew Negev, and "the Lowland" translates the Shephelah, the western foothills of Judah.
notes.7:12: The Hebrew word rendered "flint" (shamir) refers to an exceedingly hard stone such as adamant or emery.
notes.8:4: The Hebrew term rendered "squares" denotes the broad open plazas and public thoroughfares of the city.
notes.8:12: Literally "the seed of peace," signifying peaceful and abundant sowing under the LORD's renewed favor.
notes.8:19: These four fasts commemorated the stages of Jerusalem's downfall: the breaching of the walls in the fourth month, the destruction of the temple in the fifth, the assassination of Gedaliah in the seventh, and the start of the siege in the tenth.
notes.9:1: Literally "to the LORD belongs the eye of mankind," expressing either that mankind's eyes are directed toward the LORD or that the LORD's watchful eye is upon all humanity and Israel.
notes.9:6: The Hebrew term mamzer denotes one of illegitimate or mixed birth, used here for a foreign or mixed population settling in Ashdod.
notes.9:9: The Hebrew participle rendered "victorious" (nosha) literally means "saved" or "endowed with salvation," portraying the King as delivered by God and bringing deliverance.
notes.9:13: The Hebrew name Javan is the traditional biblical designation for Greece and the Ionian peoples.
notes.9:17: The masculine singular pronoun "His" may refer either to the LORD Himself or to His restored people and land described in the preceding verse.
notes.10:3: The Hebrew term for male goats is a biblical metaphor for prominent leaders, and the verse plays on two senses of the same verb: the LORD will punish the false leaders because He has visited His flock with care.
notes.10:6: The Masoretic verb translated "I will bring them back" is a rare blended form combining the roots for "return" and "settle," conveying both return from exile and secure resettlement.
notes.10:11: "The sea of distress" echoes Israel's ancient Exodus through the sea, paired with the drying up of the Nile to depict a new deliverance from oppression.
notes.11:2: Ketiv/Qere variant: the Ketiv reads "fortified" or "inaccessible," while the Qere reads a form associated with "vintage" or "impenetrable"; the translation follows the Qere in the sense of a dense, impenetrable forest.
notes.11:7: The Masoretic Text reads "indeed, the afflicted of the flock" (matching verse 11). The symbolic staff names Favor and Union represent the Hebrew terms for "delight" or "beauty" and "bonds."
notes.11:13: The Masoretic Text reads "the potter." The phrase "that magnificent price" is sharp divine irony for thirty pieces of silver, the compensation paid for a gored slave in Exodus 21:32.
notes.11:17: The Hebrew participles for "shepherd" and "who forsakes" carry poetic archaic endings rather than first-person singular possessive suffixes.
notes.12:1: The Hebrew noun translated "burden" denotes a weighty prophetic oracle or solemn pronouncement.
notes.12:2: The concise Hebrew phrasing of the second clause indicates that Judah as well will be caught up in the siege directed against Jerusalem.
notes.12:10: The Masoretic Text explicitly reads first-person "look upon Me" before shifting to third-person "mourn for Him," closely identifying the LORD with the one who is pierced.
notes.13:5: The rare Hiphil verb hiqnani literally means "acquired me" or "made me a bondservant," indicating lifelong servitude to a landowner; some traditions understand it as "taught me to tend livestock."
notes.13:6: Literally "between your hands," a Hebrew idiom referring to the chest, back, or upper body.
notes.13:8: Hebrew pi-shenayim literally means "a portion of two," denoting two-thirds in contrast with "the third" that remains.
notes.14:2: The Masoretic qere reads tishakhavnah ("shall be lain with," a euphemism for being violated), substituted in reading for the coarser ketiv verb of the same meaning.
notes.14:5: The Masoretic Text shifts abruptly to direct second-person address ("with You") referring to the LORD; "holy ones" denotes the heavenly host attending His coming.
notes.14:6: The Masoretic qere reads the noun veqippaon ("and frost" or "congealing") alongside yeqarot ("brightness"), whereas the ketiv reads the verb yiqpaun ("the bright luminaries shall congeal/diminish").
notes.14:18: The Hebrew phrase velo alehem ("and not upon them") is elliptical, supplying "rain" from verse seventeen before declaring that the plague will nevertheless strike Egypt.
notes.14:21: Hebrew kenaani literally means "Canaanite," a term also used in biblical Hebrew to mean "trader" or "merchant."
